items.title: Library supplement: Gaussian integration by parts on its integrable domain

items.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure, and let \(\gamma=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\). Fix a function \(f:E\to\mathbb R\) that is Fréchet differentiable everywhere and any direction \(v\in E\). Assume that each of \(f\), \(x\mapsto\langle x,v\rangle f(x)\), and \(x\mapsto Df(x)[v]\) is absolutely integrable under \(\gamma\). Then the weighted value and the directional derivative have the same Gaussian integral. No positive-dimension or unit-direction restriction is imposed.
assumptions: \(E\) is a real inner-product normed space of finite dimension, with its Borel measurable structure. Its completeness is derived.
\(\gamma\) is the actual centered Gaussian probability with identity covariance on \(E\).
\(f:E\to\mathbb R\) is Fréchet differentiable at every point, and \(v\in E\) is arbitrary, including zero.
\(\int_E|f|\,d\gamma<\infty\), \(\int_E|\langle x,v\rangle f(x)|\,d\gamma<\infty\), and \(\int_E|Df(x)[v]|\,d\gamma<\infty\). All three belong to this theorem’s stated domain.

bindings.boundary: This theorem supplies an equality on its stated integrable domain. It does not establish that domain for every Gaussian observable. No global Lipschitz, compact-support or additional decay assumption is introduced. Zero direction and zero dimension are allowed.
